course_title: One Health: Diseases at the Human-Animal interface

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse the biological, ecological, and socio-economic contexts of complex health threats to evaluate drivers of disease emergence and persistence.
Evaluate the roles, perspectives, and governance responsibilities of multisectoral stakeholders engaged in One Health challenges.
Apply systems thinking principles and analytical tools to evaluate the structure and dynamics of complex One Health systems and formulate feasible interventions.
Demonstrate effective communication (oral and written), collaborative teamwork, and reflective practice in transdisciplinary contexts.

assessments.task_description:
Students are required to analyse a specific One Health scenario and produce a presentation at the end of the intensive week that includes a systems model to analyse the situation and describe intervention/leverage points with a multisectoral response action plan.

See the Task Sheet on the course Learn.UQ site for further detail.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Groups will submit their presentation slides via the submission link on the Learn.UQ site.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.additional_info: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.

assessments.task_description:
Students will complete a structured critique of an article that describes a One Health problem and its resolution using the instructions and template provided on the course Learn.UQ site. Work to complete the assessment task will begin during the intensive teaching period.

The assessment mark is based on the mark given for the submitted template.

See the Task Sheet on the course Learn.UQ site for further detail.
assessments.submission_guidelines: The One Health Article Critique must be submitted using the Turnitin link provided on the course Learn.UQ site.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.due_date:
11/01/2027 - 13/01/2027

Oral examinations will be scheduled between 9am and 4.30pm on each of the days in this period, with the number of days available determined by the number of enrolments. Students will choose a times on a first come first serve basis. In-person examination is preferred.
assessments.task_description:
Each student will participate in an oral examination that comprises an initial three (3) questions aligned with Learning Outcomes 1-3 and three (3) additional critical inquiry questions. Questions must respond to one of three One health problems provided. The One Health problems and initial 3 questions are provided in the assessment task sheet at the start of the course. The additional questions will not be disclosed prior to the examination. No course notes or pre-prepared materials may be used during the oral examination. 

The oral examination will comprise 6 questions - 3 of which are provided, 3 are not provided.

Further information and examination questions will be provided on the course Learn.UQ site.
